distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.1858 +/- 0.0248 mas (same row, RUWE 0.96): 161.66 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 5.933 (5.813 to 6.054) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source): 4,127,782 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 2.100 (1.949 to 2.165) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5190 +/- 4.3 K from Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 5079636934554540160: teff_gspphot 5189.572 K (16th-84th percentiles 5185.417-5194.0493), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 5079636934554540160: teff_gspphot 5189.572 K (16th-84th percentiles 5185.417-5194.0493), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/ayeyarwady.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 3.214, rounded to two decimals
